_doc: Series the automatic ladder cannot see. Keyed on work.work_key.
_why: A series is a fact about the world, not something to compute. docs/info/isbn-ladder.md §4.4 records the shape of the mistake this file prevents: a wrong answer that scores 1.0 and has nothing textual to distinguish it from a right one. When the ladder in scripts/backfill-series.mjs cannot see a series and you know it, record it here rather than widening a regex until it fires.
_shape: "<work_key>": { "series": "Cradle", "index": 1, "display": "Book 1", "verdict": "series", "confidence": "high", "source": ["…"], "note": "…" }  — index may be null for a volume with no place on a number line (an Extra, a compilation, a sampler); display is what the cover actually says. Only `series`, `index` and `display` are read by the backfill; the rest is provenance for the next person.
_key: The work_key is normaliseTitle(title) + '|' + normaliseTitle(primaryAuthor). Read it out of the database rather than deriving it by hand: `SELECT work_key, title FROM work WHERE title LIKE '%…%'`.
_warning: ⚠️ Entries here override every other rung, including the audiobook catalog's own curated series column. That is the point, and it is also why a wrong entry here is invisible: nothing will contradict it. Every entry therefore carries a `source`. An entry with no source is a bug, not a shortcut.
_verdict: Three values, and the difference matters. `series` — the book is in a series and it is named below; the backfill writes it. `standalone` — the book was researched and genuinely belongs to no series; `series` is null, the backfill writes nothing, and the entry exists so nobody researches it a second time. `unknown` — researched and not settled; also writes nothing, and the note says what was tried. Absence from this file means nobody has looked.
_measured: 2026-08-10. The 2026-08-10 backfill left 37 works with no series. All 37 were researched: 24 got a series, 11 are true standalones, 2 remain unknown. Sources in order of strength — the EPUB's own metadata and text, the audiobook catalog's curated `series` column, Open Library *edition* records (the search index's `series` field is empty for every one of these; the edition records are not), then the publisher's or retailer's own series label.
_openlibrary: ⚠️ openlibrary.org/search.json returns `series: null` for all 37 of these, including books whose series is beyond doubt. The data is in the per-edition records: /works/<key>/editions.json, fields `series` and `subtitle`. Anything that concludes 'Open Library does not know' from the search endpoint alone is reading the wrong endpoint.
